Proposed decisions and feedback traceability

This register makes first-HTML assumptions explicit. Existing accepted decisions remain historical; the new web page plan is proposed and authorized for planning, not individually owner-approved. Developer refinement can change visual treatment; changes to authority, grading, privacy or scope must be called out.

Questions that remain for owner/institution

The HTML can use the proposed defaults while showing alternate scenarios. Before production, confirm: first institution and source roles; exact TA authoring/moderation permissions; upload formats/size and accessible alternatives; late penalties/dropped work/extra credit/rounding and letter boundaries; category and course-total publication; group membership/individual-grade disputes; quiz expiry/resume/accommodation policy; course archive/retention/download policy; meeting and reminder source authority; actual tool licenses; accessibility support path; and whether achievements or AI merit inclusion.

These questions do not block making the first HTML from this brief. They must not be disguised as universal rules or customer-validated requirements. Keep a decision log if the receiving developer changes a proposed default.

Readiness and non-goals

“All pages specified” is a handoff completeness check, not proof all product questions are solved. Competitor help pages and source inspection cannot establish market demand, ease of use, legal compliance, browser accessibility, real upload reliability or grade passback correctness. The developer should flag missing requirements discovered while implementing and add them to a revised catalogue, keeping scope/count changes explicit.
